title: 2002 HMMT February Guts Problem 21
statement: The Dyslexian alphabet consists of consonants and vowels. It so happens that a finite sequence of letters is a word in Dyslexian precisely if it alternates between consonants and vowels (it may begin with either). There are 4800 five-letter words in Dyslexian. How many letters are in the alphabet?

solutions.text: 12 Suppose there are consonants, \(v\) vowels. Then there are \(c \cdot v \cdot c \cdot v \cdot c+\) \(v \cdot c \cdot v \cdot c \cdot v=(c v)^{2}(c+v)\) five-letter words. Thus, \(c+v=4800 /(c v)^{2}=3 \cdot(40 / c v)^{2}\), so \(c v\) is a divisor of 40 . If \(c v \leq 10\), we have \(c+v \geq 48\), impossible for \(c, v\) integers; if \(c v=40\), then \(c+v=3\) which is again impossible. So \(c v=20\), giving \(c+v=12\), the answer. As a check, this does have integer solutions: \((c, v)=(2,10)\) or \((10,2)\).
